The workflow correctly qualifies the composite context; WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) as written does not. findings.mitigation: Amend WP-SCP-020 §4 020B criterion (xi) to state the full composite context format ({calling-job-name} / scp/policy-check) and require 020D2 to use the empirically verified combined string from 020E.a canary evidence before configuring branch protection. Outside 020B scope_boundary; load-bearing tracked-forward item to 020D2 dispatch-package. No code change required for 020B.

findings.claim: The single-bypass-per-invocation behaviour is not documented. Workflow lines 244-250 select only the first deny finding's rule_id; lines 369-371 filter only that rule_id from effective_denies. PRs with multiple concurrent deny findings will observe bypass-gate pass for rule 1 but workflow failure for rule 2, with no documented explanation. Fix-round-3 did not add documentation or alter the selection logic.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 244-250: for loop over policy-findings.json exits via SystemExit(0) after printing the first deny finding's rule_id. Lines 369-371: effective_denies = [item for item in denies if not (bypass_approved and bypass_rule_id and item.get('rule_id') == bypass_rule_id)] filters only the single SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID. Fix-round-3 changes were confined to verify-bypass-pairing.sh lines 33 and 105; no workflow comment or ADOPT-001 tracked-forward item was added. Gap persists since R1.
findings.impact: An adopter with two concurrent deny findings (e.g., SCP-R-001 and SCP-R-003) who activates scp_bypass=true and provides a valid waiver for SCP-R-001 will see: bypass gate passes; workflow still fails because SCP-R-003 remains in effective_denies. The SCP-E004 annotation reports bypass active 'until {expires_at}' while the check fails — diagnosable only with knowledge of the undocumented single-bypass-per-invocation constraint.
findings.mitigation: Add a workflow comment after line 250: '# Bypass covers only the first deny finding; PRs with multiple concurrent deny findings require each rule to be addressed independently or sequentially.' Add a tracked-forward note to the 020H dispatch-package requiring ADOPT-001 §12 to document single-bypass-per-invocation semantics explicitly. Non-blocking for 020B merge; the 020H documentation dependency is the load-bearing tracked-forward item.

A regression in shape 2 would not surface until 020C.1 ships waiver-aware Rego evaluation. Fix-round-3 did not add shape-2 coverage.
